newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-CHILAVERT UNABLE TO STOP INDEPENDIENTE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHILAVERT UNABLE TO STOP INDEPENDIENTE.

text.p: Goalkeeper-cum-striker Jose Luis Chilavert was unable to stop revitalised Independiente from winning their third straight match in the Argentine Aperturua championship at the weekend.

Independiente, who have looked a different team since Argentina's former World Cup coach Cesar Luis Menotti took over just before the tournament began, won 3-2 away to Chilavert's Velez Sarsfield, the reigning champions.
The Paraguayan, who scored from a free kick to earn his country a 1-1 draw away to Argentina in a World Cup qualifier last week, was beaten three times in the first half.
Chilavert, who has made a habit of scoring from free kicks and penalties, was also out of luck at the other end, failing to hit the target from his one free kick attempt.
On Thursday, an Argentine court gave Chilavert a three-month suspended prison sentence and banned him from soccer for 13 months for his part in a brawl during a match in 1994.
However, Chilavert's lawyers immediately appealed and he will carry on playing until the new hearing takes place.
Argentine Football Association president Julio Grondona, meanwhile, said that he had not been officially informed of the ban.
"It's strange that the press knew about the ban before myself and my lawyers," Chilavert said before the game.
"It bothers a lot of people that I am the best. But they're the sort who think that Paraguayans should be on a building site or cleaning people's homes."
"If they ban me, I will not stop playing because I will go abroad for a year and then I will return to carry on preventing and scoring goals."
The result left Independiente clear leaders of the Apertura championship, the first of the two tournaments which will be played in the 1996/7 season.
Boca Juniors, who have spent a reported $15 million on reinforcements, slumped to their second successive defeat as they were beaten 3-1 by modest Lanus.
